messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

country.description: The country where the museum is located, optional parameter. Default: 'USA'

message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1799–1849) | Swedish | Pioneered pointe work; famed for “La Sylphide.” |
| **Jean Coralli** (1797–1868) | Italian | Co‑director of Paris Opera Ballet; choreographed “Giselle.” |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of Imperial Russian Ballet; created “Swan Lake,” “The Sleeping Beauty.” |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1805–1872) | Italian | Developed “Blasis Method” for ballet technique. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned Viennese ballerina; known for virtuoso technique. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Created the Cecchetti method; influential teacher. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in late 19th century, she rose to fame in early 20th; known for “The Dying Swan.” |
| **John Cranko** (1901–1973) | German | Though later, his early training began in 19th‑century traditions. |
| **Martha Graham** (1894–1991) | American | Developed modern dance; her roots trace back to 19th‑century ballet. |

These dancers shaped ballet and modern dance, influencing technique, choreography, and performance standards that continue to resonate today.
